summary:
**COSMIC LEGACY** is an interactive educational web platform designed to bring attention to the forgotten equipment and technologies left behind during space exploration missions.

We developed a digital experience where users can explore space missions, discover the stories behind abandoned spacecraft and instruments, and follow interactive historical timelines.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming information about NASA's discarded and inactive equipment into accessible, engaging, and easy-to-understand content. Instead of seeing these objects as useless remains, we highlight their scientific purpose, technological achievements, and contribution to space exploration.

COSMIC LEGACY is important because every piece of equipment represents human curiosity, innovation, and the effort to explore beyond our planet. By making these stories accessible, we aim to inspire new generations to learn about space science and understand that even when a mission ends, its legacy lives on.
details:
COSMIC LEGACY: The Machines We Left Behind

COSMIC LEGACY is an interactive educational web platform that explores the history of space missions to the Moon, Mars, and other destinations. It gives visibility to the spacecraft, instruments, and technologies that remain inactive or abandoned after their missions, showing that even when they are no longer in use, they remain part of the history of space exploration.

The platform allows users to explore 13 space missions, discover 15 hardware components through a searchable library, follow a timeline featuring 40 historical milestones, and test their knowledge through an interactive quiz. It also includes a solar system explorer, detailed mission profiles, and a crew section. The entire experience is available in both Spanish and English.

We developed the application using HTML5, CSS3, and pure JavaScript, without external frameworks or a build process. The original interface was designed in Figma, while Claude supported code development and implementation. We also used Python 3 to download and prepare resources for offline access. Additional tools included Canva for graphic design, Audacity for audio recording, and Kdenlive for video editing.

Our creative approach transforms technical and historical information into an engaging, visual, and accessible experience. We considered educational accessibility, bilingual content, responsive design, ease of navigation, and offline functionality.

Our goal is to make the legacy of space exploration easier to discover, inspire curiosity in new generations, and help people understand that the end of a mission does not mean the end of its story.
